[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Direct L1 and L2 absolute or systemic bioavailability measurements for the fluoroquinolone class are all above the 20% threshold: levofloxacin approaches 100% (C12, C15), ofloxacin approaches 100% (C07, C29), trovafloxacin is 87.6% (C03, C10, C23), moxifloxacin is 86 to 99% (C04, C42), and norfloxacin has a mean of 40% (C20).

L4 absorption records show near-complete oral absorption for the class: levofloxacin is almost completely absorbed (C127), ofloxacin is 85 to 95% absorbed (C108, C113, C128), and ciprofloxacin shows 78% proximal absorption with estimated fraction absorbed above 80% (C98, C120).

L5 efflux evidence shows fluoroquinolones are P-gp, BCRP, and MRP2 substrates (C191, C162, C194, C182, C188), but direct class F values already include this efflux and remain above 20%, so efflux alone does not establish F below 20%.

L6 hepatic clearance evidence shows low-to-moderate intrinsic clearance for fluoroquinolones: an aminopyrrolidine fluoroquinolone structurally similar to the query has HLM CLint of 33.49 µL/min/mg with a 41 minute half-life and enhanced metabolic stability (C239, C218, C221), levofloxacin has the lowest CLint in the class rank order (C240), ciprofloxacin has low hepatic plasma clearance (C206), and moxifloxacin has low hepatocyte CLint (C211, C244).
Trovafloxacin undergoes UGT-mediated acyl-glucuronidation (C197, C201, C207) yet retains 87.6% oral bioavailability (C03), showing that hepatic conjugation does not drive fluoroquinolone F below 20%.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement exists for the exact query molecule.
No query-specific hepatic clearance or metabolic stability assay is available; L6 records are for other fluoroquinolones and some non-human systems.
The magnitude of hepatic first-pass loss for the query is unknown, but class-level F values already include first-pass effects and remain above 20%.
No query-specific formulation, dose, or prandial-state data are available.
The query N1 fluorocyclopropyl and C8 chlorine substituents lack direct analog bioavailability records.
content.decision_summary: L6 hepatic clearance and metabolic stability evidence is supportive: fluoroquinolones, including an aminopyrrolidine analog similar to the query, show low-to-moderate intrinsic clearance and metabolic stability (C239, C218, C221, C240, C206), and UGT glucuronidation of trovafloxacin does not prevent its 87.6% F (C197, C201, C03). This resolves the mixed metabolism prior in favor of high F. The prediction remains high with moderate confidence because no query-specific F or clearance measurement exists.
